title: Deploying Zscaler Client Connector with Microsoft Intune for macOS

blocks.text: With Microsoft Intune, you can deploy Zscaler Client Connector for your macOS devices. Before deploying Zscaler Client Connector from the Microsoft Intune admin center, download the .pkg file from the Zscaler Client Connector App Store first. The version used for the following steps is Microsoft Intune Service release version 2507.

blocks.item: Step 1: Download the Zscaler Client Connector .pkg file
To deploy Zscaler Client Connector using the Microsoft Intune admin center, you must obtain a .pkg file from the Zscaler Admin Console.
To download the Zscaler Client Connector .pkg file:
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Infrastructure > Common Resources > Deployment > Platform Releases.
On the New Releases tab, select macOS.
Download the .pkg file for the version to deploy.
Step 2: Deploy Zscaler Client Connector from the Microsoft Intune admin center
To deploy Zscaler Client Connector on your macOS devices from the Microsoft Intune admin center:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, click Apps from the menu.
In the By platform section, select macOS.
In Select app type, click macOS app (PKG).
In the App Information section, click Select app package file and upload the PKG file downloaded in the Download the Zscaler Client Connector .pkg file step.
Select file: Displays the uploaded PKG file.
Name: Enter Zscaler Client Connector X.X.X.X - macOS X.X.X.X (where X.X.X.X is the version number of the app and allows you to distinguish the version distributed by Intune).
Description: Enter Zscaler Client Connector for macOS.
Category: (Optional) Select an app category to allocate Zscaler Client Connector to.
In the Program section, configure the app installation scripts, if required.
In the requirements section, select a Minimum operating system.
Zscaler Client Connector versions 4.5.2 and later support macOS Sonoma 14.0 and later.
Included apps: Provide a list of apps included in the uploaded PKG file.
If Intune populates com.zscaler.installer.uninstall with the incorrect app version, manually correct the version.
On the Assignments tab, select the group assignments for which you want to deploy Zscaler Client Connector.
You can allocate users or groups to two different sections depending on how you want the app rolled out to users.
Required: The app is mandatory for these users and groups. The app is automatically pushed to the users of this group.

Available for enrolled devices: The app is optional for these users and groups. The app is not automatically pushed and the users can download the app themselves from the Microsoft Intune admin center.
On the Review + create tab, review the values and settings entered, and then click Create.
Step 3: (Optional) Configure a Custom Settings Profile

You can use a property list (PLIST) file to set values for various configuration keys in the Microsoft Intune admin center. To configure a custom settings profile in the Microsoft Intune admin center:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to Devices >Configuration.
In the Create a profile section:
Name: Enter a name for the preference file. For example, Zscaler Plist.

Property list file: Upload the following property list (PLIST) file. You can copy and paste the file in a Text Editor, edit Zscaler configuration parameters and their corresponding values per your organization's needs, and upload it.
In the Assignments section, choose the users, groups, and devices for the profile.
In the Review + create section, review the summary, and click Create.
Step 4: (Optional) Configure a Certificate Configuration Profile

If you use Internet & SaaS and you want to perform SSL inspection, you must configure a certificate profile to push the Certificate Authority (CA) certificate required for SSL inspection. You can use the default Zscaler CA certificate or a custom Root or Intermediate CA certificate. To learn more, see Choosing the CA Certificate for SSL Inspection and Certificate Pinning and SSL Inspection.
To configure a certificate configuration profile:
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Policies > Common Configuration > SSL/TLS Inspection > SSL/TLS Inspection Intermediate Certificate.
Click the Edit icon corresponding to the Zscaler Intermediate CA Certificate.
The Edit Zscaler Intermediate CA Certificate window appears.
In the Edit Zscaler Intermediate CA Certificate window, under the Root Certificate field, click Download.
The root certificate is downloaded as a ZIP file.
Navigate to the ZscalerRootCerts.zip file, unzip it, and rename the file extension .cer.
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to Devices > Configuration.
In the Create a profile section:
Name: Enter a name for the custom file. For example, Zscaler Root CA.
Certificate file: Upload the certificate previously downloaded.
In the Assignments section, choose the users, groups, and devices for the profile.
In the Review + create section, review the summary, and click Create.
Zscaler Client Connector can intercept traffic locally using either Route-based Interception or Transparent Proxy-based Interception.

Transparent Proxy-based Interception uses the macOS Transparent Network Proxy Extension to intercept traffic. The TRPTunnel Network Extension (com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel) is used for traffic interception and application bypass and has the following benefits:
Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 2.0 compatibility with third-party VPN clients
Removes the need for inbound firewall rules if not using machine tunnels

If machine tunnels are used with Transparent Proxy-based Interception mode enabled, inbound traffic to ZscalerTunnel must be enabled in your firewall rules to allow access to Private Access apps. In addition, be sure to disable FileVault to allow Private Access connections before a user logs in to Zscaler Client Connector on their device. To learn more, see Zscaler Client Connector Processes to Allowlist
Transparent Proxy-based Interception is supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2 and later for macOS Tahoe 26.2 and later with the following exceptions:

table: Supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later
Supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and later
Supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2.372 and later, 4.7.0.380 and later, 4.8.0.281 and later, and 4.10.0.36 and later
Supported with domain-name-based Private Access apps on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2.355 and later, 4.7.0.351 and later, and 4.8.0.252 and later

Some macOS applications have known compatibility issues with Apple's Network Extensions and you might experience interoperability issues. To learn more, see the Known Issues List on the Zscaler Support Portal.

blocks.item: When configuring Zscaler Client Connector with Transparent Proxy-based Interception, you should bypass video and audio UDP streams from collaboration applications which rely on STUN (e.g., Slack, WebEx) along with STUN using Predefined IP-Based Application Bypass, Custom IP-Based Application Bypass, or IP Exclusions in app profiles. You can bypass STUN protocol by specifying TCP and UDP port 3478.
To configure traffic interception, you must apply the following high-level steps:
Deploy a Configuration Profile to macOS Devices (Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception Only)
Follow these steps to import a preconfigured mobileconfig file into Microsoft Intune:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to Devices > Configuration.
In the Create a profile section:
Name: Enter a name for the custom file. For example, Zscaler TRP Network Extension.
Configuration profile file: Download the mobileconfig file and upload it. You can copy and paste the file in a Text Editor and edit the values per your organization's requirements.
In the Assignments tab, select the group assignments for which you want to deploy Zscaler Client Connector.
Create a Forwarding Profile and Enable Z-Tunnel 2.0
Select Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 2.0 when configuring a forwarding profile with Tunnel mode and the packet filter driver is enabled.
Configure bypasses for Z-Tunnel 2.0 in Zscaler Client Connector profile. To learn more, see Best Practices for Adding Bypasses for Z-Tunnel 2.0.

Under Forwarding Profile Action for ZIA, ensure that the Drop IPv6 in Dual Stack Network option is disabled so that IPv6 traffic isn't discarded after it has been generated by macOS, which could lead to unexpected behavior for applications and services that do not gracefully fall back to IPv4.
Create a macOS app profile or edit an existing one.
Under General, select the forwarding profile you configured in the previous step and enable the Reconnect Tunnel on System Wakeup option.
If you are configuring Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception, under Traffic Steering > Advanced, enable the Enable Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception option.
You can configure the following tunnel parameters for Zscaler Client Connector with Microsoft Intune.
This configuration setting is only supported with Route-based Traffic Interception and is not compatible with Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception.
You can use a property list (PLIST) file to set tunnel parameters, allowing DNS caching to be cleared from users' devices. To configure tunnel parameters in the Microsoft Intune admin center:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to Devices > Configuration.
In the Create a Profile section:
Name: Enter a name for the custom file.
Custom configuration profile name: Enter a profile name.
Configuration profile file: Upload the following PLIST file. You can copy and paste the file in a Text Editor and upload it.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd"> <plist version="1.0"> <dict> <key>tunnel-parameters</key> <dict> <key>clearDnsCacheOnT2Start</key> <string>1</string> </dict> </dict> </plist>
If the clearDnsCacheOnT2Start parameter is enabled, on Tunnel restart, DNS caches are cleared from the device. Enter 1 to enable, or 0 to disable.
In the Assignments tab, select the group assignments for which you want to deploy Zscaler Client Connector.
Bring Zscaler Client Connector Window to the Foreground
You can use a property list (PLIST) to set tunnel parameters, allowing you to bring the Zscaler Client Connector window to the foreground.
To bring Zscaler Client Connector window to the foreground:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to Devices > Configuration.
If you already have an existing configuration profile to control a particular Zscaler Client Connector behavior (e.g., prevent DNS caching), select the profile and click Edit.
In the Create a Profile section:
Name: Enter a name for the custom file.
Custom configuration profile name: Enter a profile name.
Configuration profile file: Upload the following property list (PLIST) file. You can copy and paste the file in a Text Editor and upload it.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd"> <plist version="1.0"> <dict> <key>tunnel-parameters</key> <dict> <key>zccToForegroundDuringAuth</key> <string>1</string> </dict> </dict> </plist>
If zccToForegroundDuringAuth parameter is enabled, it brings the Zscaler Client Connector window to the foreground during WebView-based authentication. Enter 1 to enable, or 0 to disable.
In the Assignments tab, select the group assignments for which you want to deploy Zscaler Client Connector.
Step 7: (Optional) Configure a Custom VPN Profile for Private Access VPN (for Legacy Apps)

This configuration setting is supported with Route-based Traffic Interception on all supported releases of Zscaler Client Connector for macOS and with Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later for macOS.
You can use a mobileconfig file to configure a custom VPN profile for Private Access VPN (for Legacy Apps) in the Microsoft Intune admin center:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to Devices > Configuration.
In the Create a Profile section:
Name: Enter a name for the custom file.
Custom configuration profile name: Enter a profile name.
Configuration profile file: Download the ZscalerSampleMobileConfig file and upload it.
In the Assignments tab, select the group assignments for which you want to deploy Zscaler Client Connector.
Step 8: (Optional) Configure Full Disk Access for Endpoint DLP
Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) requires full disk access for proper operation. To create a DLP profile with Microsoft Intune to allow full disk access for Endpoint DLP:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to Devices.
From the options, select Configuration > Create > New Policy.
In the Create a profile section:
Name: Enter a name for the settings catalog. For example, Endpoint DLP Settings.
In the Configuration settings section, click Add settings.
Configure the following settings using the Settings picker:
In the Browse by category section, scroll down to Privacy.
Under the Setting name section, expand Services > System Policy All Files.
Select System Policy All Files and Allowed.
In the Browse by category section, scroll down to User Experience.
Under the Setting name section, expand the Notification Settings section, and select the Notification Settings checkbox. The applicable options are automatically selected.
On the left-side navigation, configure the settings for the profiles you added in the previous step:
Under System Policy All Files, click Edit Instance.
In the Privacy Preferences Policy Control section, add the following three identifiers and configure settings for these identifiers.

table: identifier "com.zscaler.zdp.pd" and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = PCBCQZJ7S7

identifier "com.zscaler.zdp.esd" and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = PCBCQZJ7S7

identifier "com.zscaler.zep.at" and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = PCBCQZJ7S7

blocks.item: In the Notifications section, configure the settings under the Notification Settings section.
Click Edit instance. In the window that opens on the right, add the following details:
Alert Type: Select Persistent Banner from the drop-down menu.
Leave all other settings as they are.
You can configure managed login items to prevent users from disabling Zscaler Client Connector on their own devices. To configure managed login items in the Microsoft Intune admin center:
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to Devices.
From the options, select Configuration > Create > New Policy.
In the Create a profile section:
Name: Enter a name for the settings catalog. For example, Start Client Connector on Login.
In the Configuration settings section, click Add settings.
In the Settings picker, under Browse by category, search for Managed Login Item.
Select Login > Service Managed - Managed Login Items.
Under Setting name, select the Rules checkbox.
On the left-side navigation, click Edit Instance to configure the settings for the rule you added in the previous step.
Configure each of the following additional rules under Configure Instance. Enter PCBCQZJ7S7 for Team Identifier.
Bundle Identifier Prefix: A part of the bundle identifier reflecting the developer or organization.
Label: A descriptive name for an app or an element in the app's UI or settings.
Label Prefix: Used to group or categorize labels.
Team Identifier: A unique identifier for the developer team or organization within the Apple ecosystem. Applies to all of the configured rules. Enter PCBCQZJ7S7.
Rule comment: (Optional) Enter a comment for the rule.
In the Scope tags section, add tags for particular devices and users.
On the Assignments tab, select the group assignments for which you want to assign the app configuration policy, and then click Next.
In the Scope tags section, add tags for particular devices and users.
On the Assignments tab, select the group assignments for which you want to assign the app configuration policy, and then click Next.

Zscaler Client Connector supports configuring process-based application bypasses differently based on whether you intercept traffic using Route-based Interception or Transparent Proxy-based Interception and the Zscaler Client Connector version you use.

table: Set up in the Zscaler Admin Console

blocks.item: To add process-based application bypasses for macOS, use one of the following options based on the type of traffic interception and version of Zscaler Client Connector you use:
Deploy application bypass with Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception (Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later)
To configure applications to bypass in the Zscaler Admin Console:
Define any applications and process that need to be bypassed. To learn more, see Adding Process-Based Applications to Bypass Traffic.
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Infrastructure > Connectors > Client > macOS.
On the App Profiles tab, click the Edit icon on the app profile you created in step 5.
Under Traffic Steering > App and IP Bypass > Global Bypasses, select the applications to bypass from the Process-Based Application Bypass using AdminUI drop-down menu.

Deploy application bypass with Route-based Traffic Interception (all Zscaler Client Connector versions) or Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception (Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and earlier)

Application Bypass is deployed using the VPN payload in a configuration profile and because the VPN payloads are different for Route-based Traffic Interception and Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception, the mobileconfig files differ based on traffic interception type in use.

You can use bundle identifiers for application identification. If your identifier has both a Team ID and a Bundle ID in it, enter them in the format <Team ID>.<Bundle ID>. For example: <string>UBF8T346G9.com.microsoft.teams</string>

To enter multiple processes or applications, you can add all the bundle identifiers using an array. As an example, to bypass all Zoom processes, modify the downloaded mobileconfig file's BypassAppProcesses key with the following:

If you use Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception, you can also use process paths for application identification (e.g., /opt/homebrew/Cellar/podman/5.7.0/libexec/podman/gvproxy). Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2.121 and later for macOS and version 4.7.0.87 and later for macOS.
To configure a custom settings profile in the Jamf Pro Portal for the applications you want to bypass:
Step 1: Deploy a Configuration Profile to macOS Devices
Step 2: Enable Application Bypass in App Profiles
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Infrastructure > Connectors > Client > macOS.
On the App Profiles tab, click the Edit icon on the app profile you created in step 5.
Under Traffic Steering > App and IP Bypass > Global Bypasses, enable the Process-Based Application Bypass using MDM option.
Download one of the following files as a starting template, and edit the values in the <VendorConfig> section of the file based on your needs.
ZscalerSampleMobileConfig (Route-based) file for Route-based Traffic Interception
ZscalerSampleMobileConfig (Transparent Proxy-based) file for Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception
In the Microsoft Intune admin center, go to Devices.
In the Create a profile section:
Name: Enter a name for the custom file. For example, Zscaler Client Connector App Bypasses.
Custom configuration profile name: Enter the profile name.
Deployment channel: Choose a channel for deployment.
Configuration profile file: Upload the mobile config file.
In the Assignments section, choose the users, groups, and devices for the profile.
In the Review + create section, review the summary, and click Create.
